properties.Description: Canal Park is a tourist and recreation-oriented district of Duluth, Minnesota, United States. Situated across the Interstate 35 freeway from Downtown Duluth, it is connected by the famous Aerial Lift Bridge to the Park Point sandbar and neighborhood.

The Aerial Lift Bridge is a landmark in the port city of Duluth, Minnesota. The span began life in 1905 as the United States' first transporter bridge. In 1929-30, the span was converted to a vertical lift bridge, and continues to operate today.
Recreational mountain featuring wintertime downhill skiing & a summertime adventure park.
Glensheen, the Historic Congdon Estate is a 20,000 square foot mansion in Duluth, Minnesota, operated by the University of Minnesota Duluth as a historic house museum.

The Great Lakes Aquarium opened in 2000 and is located on the Duluth waterfront. A 501 private nonprofit, its mission is to inspire people to explore their connection to Lake Superior and waters of the world.
Jay Cooke State Park is a state park of Minnesota protecting the lower reaches of the St. Louis River, located about 10 miles southwest of Duluth.
Seasonal narrated train tours follow a historic transport corridor for short, long & themed rides.
Enger Park rests above Duluth's West End on a site once called Grand Mountain. The park includes the American-Japanese Peace Bell, a gift from Duluth's sister city of Ohara-Isumi.
The Lake Superior Zoo is the only zoo in Northeastern Minnesota and Northwestern Wisconsin, and the 19th oldest zoo in the United States.
Park Point is a popular summer destination for swimming and recreation with sand volleyball courts and multiple pavilions and grills.
